title: Three-Dimensional and Comprehensive Model Validation
---

**Background:** Universal ordinary differential equations (UODEs) can parameterize warm-rain formation processes by training directly on time series of bulk prognostic variables generated by super-droplet models.

**Question / Future Work:** Future research must investigate whether the proposed analytical warm-rain parameterization improves large-eddy simulations, numerical weather prediction, and climate models, and determine if similar UODE approaches can be successfully applied to more comprehensive cloud microphysics schemes including additional processes like sedimentation and evaporation.

**Why It Matters:** Evaluating whether machine-learning-derived microphysical closures translate to improved predictive skill in operational weather and climate models is a critical bottleneck in scientific machine learning for Earth sciences.

**Evidence:** Future work should therefore investigate whether the proposed analytical reformulation improves simulations in large-eddy, numerical weather prediction, and climate models, and whether similar UODE approaches can be applied to more comprehensive cloud microphysics schemes.
